decision: S1c adds test::* workspace/process/evidence operations to can.std.test@1 as opaque handles with keyed process dispatch: test::workspace_open mints an opaque workspace handle (relative-path file ops, close seals + cleans); test::run_tool dispatches by owner-registered tool key with argv/cwd/env/options (unknown keys reject pre-spawn; no paths in calls); test::evidence_open/append/seal manage an opaque bundle handle yielding digests plus a closed-vocabulary receipt kind. All three follow the S1a discipline (inventory-is-allowlist, forged fails table lookup, stale fails liveness) and the S1b server-only !browser precedent.
interpretation: Three fresh phrasings unanimously favor keyed_dispatch (1.00, 0.99, 0.98), opaque_handle workspace (0.97, 1.00, 0.98) and bundle_handle evidence (0.95, 0.92, 0.84). Agreement is advisory only; the choice is independently supported by the P28 acceptance requirement that arbitrary dispatch/eval be unrepresentable (only keyed dispatch achieves this while expressing staged offline runs), by the CORE-034 descendant-cleanup obligation binding naturally to owner-held handles, and by the row_map closed receipt vocabulary. It does not prove correctness or remove bias, and authorizes no execution or qualification.
